findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached FLOWR endpoint VJP, so coordinate contrasts are not physical interaction energies or affinity-head derivatives.

The observed support is the learning window [0.0,0.5] with 50 observed score times at 0.01 spacing, and the curve-support selection rule retained 24 features under a fidelity rule (relative RMSE <= 0.35, zero strong sign-conflict nodes, quiet-node large-fit fraction <= 0.1); this bounds which contrast curves are usable and forbids extrapolation beyond the observed window.

Continuous contrast features show sign changes and rate reversals across the observed window (e.g. landmark_00_soft_mass has 4 sign changes with first_rate_z positive and last_rate_z negative; landmark_00_local_dy has 6 sign changes with a large negative first rate and positive last rate), and no polynomial fit is accepted, so a constant rule is not supported and any time-conditioned rule must be restricted to observed-node interpolation.

The information audit reports 14 independent batches and explicitly limits interpretation: the geometric nearest-teacher comparison is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian, nonnegative excess distance is by construction rather than a causal affinity effect, and teacher score correlations are observational, not a validated affinity predictor.

Lineage support shows 14 complete survival batches but heavy ancestral sparsity (349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors, 531 with fewer than 6) and terminal metadata at score time 0.99 / state time 1.0 outside the observed window; multiple testing is BH over 400 survival field/measure tests and is explicitly not terminal affinity effects, so last-record survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

hypotheses.falsifier: the time-conditioned rule shows no improvement over the constant rule on held-out observed nodes, or the feature's sign conflicts exceed the fidelity rule
hypotheses.observable: sign and magnitude of the selected continuous contrast feature at observed score nodes
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast rule that follows the observed sign of a validated continuous contrast feature (e.g. landmark_00_soft_mass) within the observed window will track the endpoint pointcloud reward better than a constant rule, because the supplied curves show sign changes and rate reversals with no accepted polynomial.

hypotheses.falsifier: selection and survival directions agree across batches, removing the need for separate priority treatment
hypotheses.observable: difference between selection-node contrast direction and descendant survival-credit direction
hypotheses.scope: 14 independent batches; survival credit is not final affinity
hypotheses.statement: Selection-node coordinate contrasts and later survival/quality credit may disagree, and that disagreement should reorder direction priorities rather than be averaged, because ancestral coverage is sparse and survival multiple testing is not terminal affinity.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied; last-record survival credit is not final affinity benefit and the terminal comparison is unavailable.
Continuous contrast curves are coordinate features in predicted endpoint world coordinates, not physical interaction energies or evidence of neural-module causation.
No current-study outcome data are available to the Analyst, so no claim about realized affinity improvement can be made.
Turnover, moment, pair-kernel and joint-motif diagnostics were not read in this pass and remain unassessed.
